MirrorFinding.description:
One difference between the registry and MLflow. `pending`: a sync will fix it. `drift`: an
unrequested change to a platform-owned part; only a reconcile repairs it. `conflict`: not
platform-owned or ambiguous; never changed.

MirrorSummary.description:

whether MLflow has caught up. `disabled` unless `AUTOML_REGISTRY_MIRROR=on`.

RegisterRequest.description:
Register a sealed package as the next version of a model. Give a `package_id`, a `job_id`
(a succeeded final job), or both; if both, they must name the same package.
RegisterRequest.title: RegisterRequest

status.description: `ok`: a drift verdict was reached. `insufficient_data`: too few rows, no verdict. `failed`: the run broke (see `error`); never a success.

summary.description: Feature drift, dataset-drift share, prediction drift, performance, rules.

state.title: State

post.description: Compares the most recent logged predictions of this deployment (one traffic scope: real by default, or simulated; never mixed) with its reference sample: per-feature drift, the dataset-drift share, prediction drift, and live performance against the stored offline value. Stores an immutable report and updates alerts. Below `min_rows` rows the report says `insufficient_data` and reaches no verdict; a run that breaks is stored as `failed`, never as a success; neither opens or resolves an alert. Drift means inputs or predictions differ from the training sample, not that the model is wrong. Needs a reference sample (409 `no_reference`). One run per deployment at a time (409 `monitoring_in_progress`).

get.description: Computed on demand with the same metric code as the offline evaluation, but only over predictions that have a true value (`POST /feedback` on the serving app). Unlabelled predictions are counted and excluded. With fewer than `min_labelled` labelled predictions you get a status and the counts, not metrics. `scope` chooses real traffic (default), simulated traffic or both. The stored offline final-test summary is returned separately in `offline_reference`; it is a different measurement and is never mixed in. Nothing here reads a dataset or the held-out test part.
